summary: Desert Mountain lookout, Flathead NF: 1919 log cabin, 1930 timber tower with 14x14 cab; destroyed 1977 per two sources, removed per a third.

facts.design: Ten-foot timber tower with a pre-cut live-in cab, 14 by 14
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1977 per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; the Weebly history says removed. WillhiteWeb photo captions show communication towers and an old footing at the site.

access.note: WillhiteWeb describes an easy drive-up road that most cars can manage in good conditions, popular with ATVs. No source states an access rule.

events.note: Ranger's crew building a trail to the summit where a lookout station was to be built
Two-story log cabin with a patrol atop Belton Point. Only firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb date this.
Fred Novak named as lookout for the fire season
Ten-foot timber tower with pre-cut 14 by 14 live-in cab, half a mile south of the summit. Cab made by Superior Building Company of Columbia Falls.
Mr. and Mrs. Melvin Yuhas reported two man-caused fires, one in Martin City (youngster's sparkler) and one up the Spotted Bear road (firecrackers or a smoker)
Station used for a cloud-breeding and jet-stream study with specially adapted cameras; manned by Mr. and Mrs. B. Harvey Kom
Latest staffing year named in the sources (Mr. and Mrs. Billy Jones). Also 1952 and 1957 couples listed.
FBI agents investigated a burglary at the tower; about $200 of government property missing; no vandalism beyond the forced entry
Destroyed per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb. The Weebly history lists it as removed with no date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say the lookout was destroyed in 1977. The Weebly history says removed, with no date. The story reports destruction in 1977 and notes the Weebly wording.

The 1919 two-story log cabin appears only on firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb. The Weebly history begins with the 1915 plan and the 1930 tower. The story gives both and does not say whether the cabin was replaced.

The history places the 1930 tower half a mile south of the summit. The visit note places the lookout structure at the south point hang-gliding site. These may be the same place, which no source confirms.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: county, status, and coordinates match the FFLOS list. Open conflicts: the 1919 cabin is only on two sources; destroyed (firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb) versus removed (Weebly); and the visit note's hang-gliding site versus the half-mile-south location. Access 'public' is inferred from the visitor's road description, not an official statement. Summit elevation differs between sources (WillhiteWeb 6,440 ft; Weebly calls it almost 7,000 ft), so it is left out. No photo records added.
